meta.title: Algolia for Nike — Search that matches your scale
meta.description: A personalized look at what Algolia AI Search could do for Nike.com, grounded in PRISM's audit of nike.com search.

hero.eyebrow: Sporting Goods & Athletic Apparel · Global Ecommerce

findings.heading: Four gaps in nike.com search today
findings.subheading: Observed directly on nike.com, not inferred.

items.title: Every visitor sees the same results
items.body: After browsing running shoes on nike.com, searching "shoes" surfaces Jordan 1 Retro High OG first — zero personalization. Algolia re-ranks results in real time using user affinity signals, integrating with Nike's existing Adobe Analytics event stream.

items.title: Natural-language queries don't fully resolve
items.body: Shoppers searching "best shoes for trail running under 150" still see $159–$160 products — the price constraint is heard but not enforced. Algolia NeuralSearch parses multi-attribute natural language and auto-applies filters as pre-applied chips.

items.title: Autocomplete has no category or content guidance
items.body: Typing "running" in SAYT shows text suggestions and 5 product thumbnails only — no "Running > Trail Shoes" category route, forcing shoppers through 152 generic results. Algolia Federated Search surfaces products, categories, content, and help articles in one ranked panel.

items.title: A dead end, not a redirect
items.body: Searching "Yeezy Boost 350" on nike.com returns the exact same zero-results page as a random keyboard smash — no competitive redirect, no cross-sell logic. Algolia's Rules Engine detects competitor-brand queries and triggers targeted merchandising instead.
